title: Tension
body:
**Tension** is the pull transmitted along a rope, string or cable. It acts along the rope and
pulls inward on whatever is attached at each end, since a rope pushes nothing.

For an ideal rope, meaning massless and inextensible over an ideal pulley, the tension is the
same everywhere along it. That is the assumption that makes a two-block problem solvable, and
it is what allows one unknown $T$ to appear in both blocks' equations:

```
two blocks joined by a rope over a pulley, m₁ hanging, m₂ on a table

  m₁:  m₁g - T = m₁a          the rope holds it back
  m₂:  T - f   = m₂a          the rope pulls it along

two equations, two unknowns, and the same T in both
```

A pulley changes the direction of the tension and leaves its magnitude alone when it is ideal.
An inextensible rope also forces both blocks to share one acceleration, which is the second
constraint the pair of equations needs.
